newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended lower again on Wednesday after initially opening firmly, as drooping bonds and investor wariness beat the market down in thin volumes, dealers said.
"It's been a pretty dull market, but the bonds are very bad and that's not good news for us," one share dealer said. "And turnover is very low, with people going back to the sidelines."

Traders said few of the major individual stocks had stood out on a day declines led advances by 18 to three. But midcap industrial company Stork thrived on news it had won a billion guilder contract to renovate a major Dutch gasfield.
Stork shares spiked to a new year high of 59.20 guilders, fully 2.00 guilders higher than their previous peak of 57.20 set on November 15, before closing at 58.60.
"I think it is a very good deal for Stork and I think the shares could well go up even further," a trader said.

Heineken also bucked the downward trend, rising 1.80 guilders after taking a beating over the last few days. Dealers said bargain hunters had been getting into the stock, thought to be close to bottoming out.
"I can't see it under 310.00 (guilders) and I suspect others feel that way too," a broker said.
Heineken closed at 314.50, from 312.70 on Tuesday, when it had fallen over 10 guilders in two days.

Dutch financials were generally weaker, including banking and insurance major ING, which reports third-quarter and cumulative nine-month results tomorrow. Analysts are looking for strongly higher profits from the group.
One broker said there seemed to be a small correction in the financials, but good ING results and momentum from still low long interest rates should see the sector advancing again soon.
Food group CSM reported net profit of 201.6 million guilders, close to expectations, shortly after the close. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
